macros.name: @D
macros.doc: \@D{⟨length⟩} is the amount to indent prior to ⟨sec-num⟩.

macros.name: @DS
macros.doc: \@DS{⟨num⟩} The ⟨num⟩ determines the separation between dots for a TOC entry that uses a dotted rule line.

macros.name: @E
macros.doc: \@E Within the minitocfmt environment, the command \@E expands to the current TOC entry number of the TOC entry being read in.

macros.name: @F
macros.doc: \@F{⟨fmt⟩} is the formatting for the title heading of the current section; for example, \@F{\bfseries} turns all heading, for this ⟨sec-name⟩, bold.

macros.name: @L
macros.doc: \@L This macro expands to the hyperref anchor of the page entry reference, it is empty if hyperref is not loaded.

macros.name: @P
macros.doc: \@P{⟨fmt⟩} is the formatting for the page number (⟨pg-num⟩).

macros.name: @Pg
macros.doc: \@Pg This macro expands to the page number this entry references.

macros.name: @PW
macros.doc: \@PW{⟨length⟩} Within the argument of \@A, you can insert \@PW{⟨length⟩} to set the width of the box that contains the page number (\@pnumwidth).

macros.name: @R
macros.doc: \@R{⟨length⟩}is a convenience command, it takes its argument and defines the LaTeX command \@tocrmarg, which sets the right margin for the sec-title.

macros.name: @W
macros.doc: \@W{⟨length⟩} is the width of the box that encloses ⟨sec-num⟩.

macros.name: declaretocfmt
macros.doc: \declaretocfmt{⟨sec-name⟩}{⟨various⟩} This command formats all ⟨sec-name⟩ (section, subsection, etc.) entries.

macros.name: mtocgobble
macros.doc: \mtocgobble is a public version of the core LaTeX command \@gobble; it simply absorbs (gobbles) its argument.

macros.name: mtoclabel
macros.doc: you can mark section commands (chapter, part, section, subsection, subsubsection, paragraph, and subparagraph) using a special label command (\mtoclabel{⟨label-name⟩}) defined by aeb-minitoc.
